pool.text: John Calvin became the spiritual leader of Geneva and established a Protestant Rome.
The Société des Vieux-Grenadiers gentlemen's club was founded to regroup the local elite.
Revolutionary France under the Directory annexed Geneva during a period of conflict.
Geneva officially joined the Swiss Confederation on the nineteenth of May.
The opera house, Grand Théâtre de Genève, officially opened in the city.
Henry Dunant became the first recipient of the prestigious Nobel Peace Prize.
The Grand Théâtre de Genève opera house was partly destroyed by a fire.
Renée Colliard triumphed as a gold medallist at the Winter Olympics.
Germaine Aussey established her permanent residence in the city of Geneva.
The Grand Théâtre de Genève opera house officially reopened following its fire.
A Franco-Swiss agreement created the Comité régional franco-genevois for regional cooperation.
Marc Rosset earned a gold medal victory at the Olympic Games.
Léman Bleu, a local TV channel distributed by cable, was founded.
An urban planning charter defined a planning territory called agglomération franco-valdo-genevoise.
A Charter for Public Transports was adopted to develop a cross-border commuter rail network.
A public transnational body called Projet d’agglomération franco-valdo-genevois was created.
The Genevan Brass Festival was founded by Christophe Sturzenegger.
The Projet d’agglomération franco-valdo-genevois was renamed Grand Genève.
The metropolitan area Geneva created an open data light pollution map featuring a dark grid.
Geneva was ranked as the world's fifteenth most important financial centre by a global index.
